Sure! Here’s an easy yet flavorful **“Tandoori‑Style Steak”** you can whip up at home. It blends classic tandoori spices with a quick pan sear so your steak gets all those smoky notes without needing a real tandoor.

---

### Ingredients  

| Item | Quantity |
|------|----------|
| Ribeye / New York Strip steak (1–2 inches thick) | 2 pieces (~200 g each) |
| Plain yogurt (Greek or regular) | ½ cup |
| Lemon juice | 1 tbsp |
| Garlic paste | 1 tsp |
| Ginger paste | 1 tsp |
| Kashmiri red chili powder (for color & mild heat) | 1 tsp |
| Garam masala | ½ tsp |
| Ground cumin | ¼ tsp |
| Ground coriander | ¼ tsp |
| Turmeric powder | ⅛ tsp |
| Salt | to taste |
| Fresh cilantro leaves | handful (chopped) |
| Butter or ghee | 1 tbsp |
| Optional: smoked paprika or liquid smoke | pinch |

> *Tip:* If you’re short on time, use store‑bought “tandoori spice mix.” Just add it instead of individual powders above.

---

### Marinade Preparation  
1. In a bowl, whisk together yogurt, lemon juice, garlic paste, ginger paste, and salt until smooth.  
2. Add Kashmiri chili powder, garam masala, cumin, coriander, turmeric, and optional smoked paprika/liquid smoke. Mix thoroughly.  
3. Pat steaks dry; place them into the bowl and coat both sides evenly. Cover and refrigerate **at least 30 minutes**, ideally 2–4 hours (overnight works great).  
   - *Why marinate?* Yogurt tenderizes while spices infuse flavor and create a nice crust when seared.

---

### Cooking Steps  

#### Option A – Pan Sear (quickest)
1. Heat a heavy skillet (cast iron preferred) over high flame until smoking hot.  
2. Drizzle butter/ghee; let it melt but don’t brown.  
3. Place steaks onto the pan—no crowding—and sear about **45 seconds per side** for medium‑rare (adjust if thicker/thinner).  
4. Flip once only; avoid pressing down.  
5. While searing, sprinkle chopped cilantro over the top for aroma.  
6. Remove from heat; tent loosely with foil and rest **5 min** before slicing.

#### Option B – Oven Finish (if you want extra char)
1. Preheat oven to 220 °C (425 °F).  
2. After initial sear (as above), transfer skillet directly to preheated oven. Bake 4–7 mins depending on thickness/desired doneness.  
3. Rest as described.

---

### Serving Suggestions  

| Side Dish | Why it Works |
|-----------|--------------|
| Mint‑Yogurt Chutney | Balances spiciness with coolness |
| Grilled Asparagus or Bell Peppers | Adds veggies & smokey char |
| Naan or Flatbread | Perfect for scooping juices |
| Simple Green Salad | Lightens meal |

Serve slices against a bed of rice pilaf or roasted potatoes for a complete plate.

---

### Quick FAQ  

| Question | Answer |
|----------|--------|
| **Can I use other cuts?** | Yes—sirloin, strip loin, even flank will work. Adjust resting time accordingly. |
| **What if I’m allergic to dairy?** | Replace yogurt with coconut milk + lime juice; keep spices same. |
| **How do I get more smoke flavour?** | Sprinkle a dash of liquid smoke during marinading or finish on grill. |

Enjoy your homemade Tandoori‑style steak—a perfect blend of Indian zest and Western technique!
